## Overview

I supervise research students working at the intersection of corpus linguistics, sociolinguistics, learner language, and computational approaches to language data. Since 2015, I have been involved in the supervision of research projects at Universität Hamburg, The University of Queensland, and the University of Zurich, in addition to serving on external PhD committees in Norway and Germany.

## Prospective Students

I welcome enquiries from prospective PhD and MPhil students, particularly in the following areas:

**Sociolinguistics, language variation and change, World Englishes**
General extenders; terms of address and salutations; discourse particles and markers; vulgarity and swearing; adjective amplification.

**Learner language, corpus phonetics, learner corpus research**
Vowel production and voice-onset time among L1 speakers and learners of English; fluency and pausing in learner and L1 speech; accent, intelligibility, and comprehension.

**Text analytics, digital humanities, corpus linguistics**
Applications of AI, large language models, and word embeddings in the language sciences; comparison of association and keyness measures; reproducible workflows for language data.

If you are interested in working with me, please [get in touch](contact.qmd) with a short outline of your proposed project (1–2 pages), your CV, and a brief description of your methodological background.


[*Link to the UQ HDR addmissions information page*](https://study.uq.edu.au/admissions/phd-mphil-professional-doctorate)
